newsitem.title: USA: Lott wants capital gains tax under 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: Lott wants capital gains tax under 20 percent.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told business leaders here that he would like to see capital gains taxes reduced to less than 20 percent from a system that has some investors paying up to 39 percent.
"We would like to see it under 20 percent," Lott told reporters following a speech outlining his goal for dismantling the U.S. tax system by 2001.
Lott said the balanced-budget agreement reached Friday between the White House and congressional Republicans was not specific on the amount of capital gains tax relief.
The Senate Finance Committee and House Ways and Means Committee will decide on cutting the capital gains tax rate within the deal's $135 billion in gross tax cuts over five years.
"I think we ought to let them look at it and what will be best for the economy," Lott said.
Lott said the committees has the option of making a capital gains tax cut retroactive. He said the only limitation on a capital gains tax cut would be within the gross tax cut numbers.
"You would have to allow room for tax credits and other components, but I think there is enough there to get it down into that range of under 20 percent," Lott said.
